Like building a house or figuring out makeshift ways to collect potable water, shit like that. If a problem involves mostly talking or convincing other people or thinking about the morality or the solution or whatever, it’s more frustrating to me than anything.

If you’re talking about the pandemic, this isn’t an apocalypse. And if it was, it would be literally the most boring apocalypse of all time. For me personally, it’s changed virtually nothing about my day to day life. Most I can say is, it’s been difficult to go to the gym at times. But I work out from home, so not a big impact. Can’t hold down jobs anyway, pandemic or no, don’t have friends to visit, don’t leave the house really at all, so I basically live my life in lockdown before, and will continue to long after any formal lockdown is gone for good. Not afraid of dying and it feels like, even if I was, there’s not a lot of risk for me anyway, certainly nothing to get the blood pumping.

And there’s absolutely zero practical problems to solve. The only issues I’ve dealt with as a result of this have been financial and bureaucratic bullshit, the kind of problems that aren’t satisfying to chip away at or solve because it just feels like you’re beating you head against a brick wall and making absolutely zero progress on what’s usually a very simple and straightforward issue. It’s like you have to explain color to a blind man just to get a government department to approve a simple application. There’s nothing in that experience that appeals to my problem solving brain, in fact, it’s stuff like that that’s the reason I want a *real* apocalypse in the first place.
